messages:
Maya Chen: Heads up — converting hf/model-x to Redwood broke some chat prompts; leading spaces and role delimiters got mangled.
Ajay Patel: repro steps?
Maya Chen: quick repro: HF tokenizer used NFKC normalization + byte-fallback; our convert tool dropped the normalizer so '  Hello' and ' Hello' map to different token streams in HF vs converted.
Leah O'Neill: can you paste the token ids / config.json snippet?
Maya Chen: snippet: ```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
print(t.encode(' Hello').tokens)
print(t.encode('\u212B').tokens)
``` With NFKC on the HF file \u212B normalizes to \u00C5 and tokens differ. Convert tool ignored normalizer.
Ajay Patel: aha — our hf_to_redwood pipeline currently strips unknown normalizer entries. The HF `tokenizer.json` has "normalizer": {"name": "NFKC"} and we weren't mapping that.
Maya Chen: impact: small but reproducible eval regression on prompt steering tests — exact-match down ~3% and PPL up ~0.7 after conversion. Also saw a handful of role tokens split across tok boundaries.
TokenOps Bot: @Maya Chen created issue #542 (tokenizer-normalizer-mismatch) and assigned to Ajay Patel.
Ajay Patel: immediate mitigation: re-run a NFKC normalizer pass at input (pre-tokenize) as a canary. Longer-term: update convert tool to translate HF normalizer -> Redwood normalizer pipeline and preserve pre_tokenizer and added_tokens.
Leah O'Neill: note: HF byte_fallback interacts with whitespace handling; removing it changes leading-space tokens which many chat templates rely on. We should have a token-boundary smoke test in onboarding.
Maya Chen: tested the input-normalize canary — it fixed the EM drop but median latency +2ms on short requests. Deployable short-term for Dedicated.
Ajay Patel: also saw a related issue: special tokens mapping (added_tokens) got lost so marker like `<|assistant|>` ended up split. I'll add a conversion step to merge added_tokens into vocabulary and preserve their ids.
Maya Chen: quick hotfix script in tickets branch: ```bash
python tools/fix_tokenizer.py --in tokenizer.json --out tokenizer.fixed.json
# copies normalizer, merges added_tokens, sets pre_tokenizer to ByteLevel if byte_fallback present
```
Leah O'Neill: one more: quantization experiments amplified these errors — int8 runs showed worse degradation because KV cache assumptions + token alignment diverged. So onboarding must include quantized vs fp32 tokenization parity checks.
Ajay Patel: agreed — I'll add unit tests to hf_to_redwood: sample 2k prompts, compare token id sequences HF vs converted, fail the convert if mismatch rate > threshold. Also map NFKC/NFKD/NFC normalizers.
Maya Chen: I'll open the PR with convert-tool changes + tests and enable NFKC canary in Dedicated.
Leah O'Neill: sounds good. Also add a line in the onboarding checklist: "verify normalizer + byte_fallback equivalence". :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: thanks — will update the eval dashboard to show token-boundary diffs for new model brings.
thread_summary: Discussion about HF->Redwood tokenizer conversion dropping normalizer entries (NFKC), byte-fallback and whitespace differences causing prompt steering regressions; immediate canary (apply NFKC pre-normalize) fixes regressions with minor latency cost; plan to update convert tool to preserve normalizer/pre_tokenizer/added_tokens and add onboarding token-boundary tests.
